# FLicc: a framework for length-interval catch curves

FLicc fits **length-interval catch curves (ICC)**: equilibrium models that
explain the length composition of the catch by growth, natural mortality,
fishing mortality and selectivity, integrated over length intervals (bins).
It brings the two main lines of length-based per-recruit assessment into one
framework, built on FLR (Kell et al. 2007) and fitted with TMB (Kristensen et
al. 2016):

- **fishblicc** (Medley 2025), whose
  formulation FLicc follows most closely: steady-state length-interval
  survival with individual Linf gamma-distributed around the von Bertalanffy
  mean, constant mortality within each length interval, several gears with
  their own selectivity (logistic, normal and double-sided normal), and a
  negative-binomial likelihood. FLicc's `pop_model = "gamma"` with
  `obs_model = "nb"` reproduces this setup ([Reproducing fishblicc](#repro-fishblicc));
  FLicc fits it by maximum likelihood in TMB instead of Bayesian estimation in
  Stan.
- **LBSPR** (Hordyk et al. 2015, 2016), whose growth-type-group (GTG)
  formulation is FLicc's default population model (`pop_model = "gtg"`): Linf
  varies between growth-type groups, each with its own survival through the
  length classes, and status is expressed as the spawning potential ratio.
- **LBB** (Froese et al. 2018), the length-based Bayesian biomass estimator,
  which is nested in the GTG model: one growth type, one gear, each year
  fitted separately, with priors on Linf and M/K. `lbb_flicc()` sets FLicc up
  as LBB, and LBB's status measure B/B0 (exploited biomass relative to
  unfished) is available for any FLicc fit as the exploitable potential ratio
  (EPR; [Reproducing LBB](#repro-lbb)).

Each of these tools is a configuration of FLicc:

| Tool | FLicc configuration |
|---|---|
| [LBSPR](#repro-lbspr) | `pop_model = "gtg"` (`ngtg = 13`, `maxsd = 2`, CVL 0.1), `obs_model = "mn"`, Linf, M/k and CVL fixed, `by_year = TRUE` |
| [LBB](#repro-lbb) | `lbb_flicc()`: `pop_model = "gtg"` with `ngtg = 1`, `obs_model = "dm"` (fixed precision; `ess = 20000` matches LBB's Dirichlet), priors on Linf and M/k, `by_year = TRUE`, `pile = 0` or `1` |
| [fishblicc](#repro-fishblicc) | `pop_model = "gamma"`, `obs_model = "nb"`, several gears, catch shares in numbers |
| FLicc default | `pop_model = "gtg"`, `obs_model = "dm"` with the precision estimated (`dm_theta = "saturating"`), all years jointly with a random walk on F |

Each configuration is reproduced on the tool's own example data, and compared
with FLicc's default, in section [Reproducing LBSPR, LBB and
fishblicc](#reproduce).

On this common basis FLicc adds what a routine assessment and management
procedure needs: several years fitted jointly with shared selectivity and a
random walk on F, alternative observation models (multinomial,
Dirichlet-multinomial with estimated precision, negative binomial), treatment
of the tail of the composition, reference points with steepness, length-based
indicators, residual diagnostics, and use as the estimation model of an MSE in
FLR.

The names of the models and options in FLicc credit these sources: fishblicc
for the length-interval catch-curve formulation, multi-gear selectivity and the
gamma growth model; LBSPR for the GTG model and the SPR-based use of length
data in data-limited fisheries; LBB for the single-growth-type special case,
its priors and the B/B0 status measure.

## About this guide

The guide is in three parts. **Part I** goes through an assessment from the
data to stock status: length-frequency data (including missing data), life
history, selectivity, fitting and diagnostics, reference points and status, and
length-based indicators, with explicit **checks** at each step (what to look
at, what is a red flag, what to do about it). **Part II** documents the
technical options for users who need them: effective sample size and
observation models, fishing mortality over time, growth variability and
life-history priors, the tail of the composition, the model equations and a
comparison of models, and the reproduction of LBSPR, LBB and fishblicc. **Part III** covers
use in management-strategy evaluation and summarises the checks and
recommendations. The examples use the built-in splendid alfonsino data.
Recommendations marked *simulation* come from tests with an alfonsino-like
operating model (fixed-CV length-at-age, annual recruitment, Beverton-Holt
h = 0.75, two gears, two-stage length sampling). Monte-Carlo ensembles over
life-history uncertainty (`mc_flicc()`) will be documented separately.
